title: The 8 Levels of The Office Party Hangover
house: A bustling metropolitan city made of giant ceramic plates and stainless steel towers where fruit and vegetable people commute on electric scooters past neon billboards displaying digital net income numbers.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.
links: A quiet voice in Level 1 mentions the barista at the neon kiosk who always hands out free lukewarm coffee.
The executive in Level 8 leaves his golden cufflinks in the taxi that picks up the intern in Level 2.
A half-eaten box of luxury donuts from the company party sits on the counter in Level 4, untouched by the CEO in Level 7.

levels.name: Pip, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 1. Level 1: 1,200 dollars a month – and I woke up wearing my boss designer blazer inside the office copy machine room. My head felt like a cement mixer. My forehead number burned bright and pathetic: 1,200 dollars. I checked my phone: forty unread messages and one very angry text from Mr. Thornberry. I spilled half my iced coffee on the floor as I tried to crawl out under the glass doors. You wore my luxury blazer to sleep on the printer, Pip, now get your pulp out of my lobby before security throws you out. I clutched my head and whispered back that I did not even remember leaving the open bar. You will pay for dry cleaning out of your next three miserable paychecks. My eyes burned with hot tears as I grabbed my crushed cardboard box of desk items. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Sunny, 26, Junior Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 2. Level 2: 2,400 dollars a month – and I found three empty tequila shots inside my desk drawer next to the tax receipts. My forehead glowed a steady, mediocre amber. I tried to type my spreadsheet, but the numbers kept dancing like drunken beetles. My senior manager walked past my cubicle with a steaming mug and a smirk that chilled my soul. You missed the quarterly review this morning because you were snoring in the breakroom, Sunny. I stammered that my alarm did not go off after the karaoke disaster. She slammed a thick red folder onto my keyboard with a deafening thud. That cost us the client meeting, and your career here is hanging by a very thin thread. I stared at her immaculate white lab coat and pristine 7,500 dollar monthly badge. My hands shook as I reached for my calculator and felt my stomach drop into my shoes. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Leo, 31, Marketing Lead
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 3. Level 3: 4,100 dollars a month – and my boss just forwarded my drunken voice note to the entire global board of directors. My forehead number flashed a nervous, bright turquoise. I dropped my pen into my lukewarm chamomile tea as my phone buzzed incessantly on the glass table. Max strode into the conference room wearing a tailored Italian suit that cost more than my car. You really poured your heart out about my leadership skills in that voice note, Leo. I felt the color drain entirely from my avocado skin. Max chuckled, swirling an expensive glass of sparkling water like a villain in a movie. The board found it hilarious, but your promotion to director is officially cancelled. I slammed my fist onto the mahogany meeting table, rattling the glass pitchers. That recording was private property taken while I was drugged at the open bar. Keep talking like that, and you will not even have a desk by tomorrow afternoon. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Maya, 29, Project Manager
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 4. Level 4: 5,800 dollars a month – and I found my resignation letter already printed out on my desk printer. My forehead number glowed a sharp, stressed orange. I picked up the warm paper and felt my knees weaken. The HR director strolled by with a condescending grin plastered across his face. We all saw you dancing on the boardroom table at two in the morning, Maya. I gripped the edges of my desk so hard my knuckles turned white. That was a private celebration for hitting our annual target two months early. Celebrating is fine, but telling the VP his hairpiece looks like a dead squirrel crossed a line. I stared at his glowing 11,200 dollar monthly badge and felt pure rage boil inside my veins. You have no proof other than a blurry photo taken by someone who hates me. He leaned down and whispered right into my ear with venomous calm. The board does not need proof when they already have your replacement waiting outside. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Oliver, 34, Senior Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 5. Level 5: 7,500 dollars a month – and I found my blueprint drafts covered in red wine stains right before the big client pitch. My forehead number glowed a confident, steady blue. I stared at the ruined architectural drawings spread across my drafting table in absolute disbelief. Clara marched into my studio holding an empty glass of vintage Merlot like a trophy. Looks like your masterpiece got a little redecorated during last night's rooftop celebration, Oliver. I clenched my jaw so hard I thought my teeth would shatter into pieces. That project took me six months of sleepless nights to design for the municipal bidding. The client hates wine stains almost as much as they hate architects who party until dawn. I stepped right into her personal space, refusing to let her intimidate me anymore. You sabotaged my desk because you knew my proposal was better than yours. Prove it in front of the board in ten minutes. My heart hammered against my ribs like a trapped bird. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Victoria, 39, VP of Finance
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 6. Level 6: 11,200 dollars a month – and my own digital signature was used to authorize a mysterious offshore bonus after the gala. My forehead number glowed a brilliant, elite silver. I stared at the audit log on my curved monitor while my coffee grew ice cold. Mr. Thornberry strolled into my private office without knocking, adjusting his expensive silk tie. I see someone had a very generous night while everyone else was asleep, Victoria. I spun my chair around to face him with absolute fury in my eyes. I was fast asleep in my penthouse by midnight, and you know my password protocol. The board does not care who typed the code; they care that your account received the payout. I stood up so fast my leather chair rolled backward into the bookshelf. You set me up because I refused to sign off on your illegal real estate acquisitions. You have forty-eight hours to return the funds or face federal embezzlement charges. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Julian, 45, Chief Operating Officer
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 7. Level 7: 18,500 dollars a month – and I found the entire corporate server backup wiped clean the morning after our annual gala. My forehead number shone a bright, commanding gold. I stood in the freezing server room while the cooling fans whined like sirens in the dark. Max stepped through the heavy metal security door holding a glass of scotch and a smug grin. Looks like someone forgot to lock the digital vault before heading to the open bar, Julian. I turned around slowly, my fists clenched inside my wool coat pockets. You locked me out of the master terminal at midnight using your executive override code. The board thinks you deleted the files to cover up your disastrous supply chain losses last quarter. I glared at him with pure venom, stepping closer despite the freezing chill. We both know you needed those files gone to hide your own offshore accounts. Prove it to the federal investigators when they arrive in twenty minutes. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Arthur, 52, Chief Executive Officer
levels.story: The 8 levels of waking up after the company party with the boss. Level 8. Level 8: 45,000 dollars a month – and I watched every single one of my employees walk into the boardroom to decide my fate after the wildest company party in history. My forehead number burned with a blinding, platinum glow. I sat at the head of the long mahogany table while all seven levels of fruit and vegetable people took their seats around me. Pip, Sunny, Leo, Maya, Oliver, Victoria, and Julian stared at me with a mixture of awe, exhaustion, and lingering hangover pain. You all thought the party was just a reckless night of mistakes and leaked voice notes. Silence fell instantly across the room as the digital clock on the wall ticked toward nine o'clock. I stood up slowly and placed the real master key right in the center of the polished wood. Last night was a test to see who would protect this company when everything fell apart. Julian slid the golden key toward himself with a slow, knowing smile that answered every lingering question. The number on your forehead might show your salary, but character is the only currency that truly matters here. Every single lie, sabotage, and framed accusation was now laid bare before the entire board. My heart raced as the final vote count began to illuminate every digital display in the room simultaneously. Which character's journey surprised you the most, and whose story should we uncover in our next series?
